description: E-commerce site went down after a sudden traffic spike caused by a marketing campaign. The outage was caused by a configuration error in cluster resource management which prevented more service instances from starting even though hardware resources were available.

A configuration change in the Seoul region incorrectly removed the setting that specifies the minimum healthy hosts for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet, so the system fell back to a very low default. The fleet's healthy host count dropped and in-VPC DNS queries from EC2 instances failed for ~84 minutes until capacity was manually restored. AWS added semantic config validation and per-hour throttling on host removal as remediations.

A deploy changed the type of a field in the PostgreSQL database used by the job-distribution service. Newly-written rows used the new type and old rows used the old type, so the distributor's strict schema validation failed on each scan and it stopped distributing work.

On 18 Nov. 2025, a change in permissions in a database in Cloudflare's bot-detection systems caused a file to be output that exceeded the limits of the software that runs that system. That file was propagated throughout Cloudflare's network, causing a systemwide outage.
A bad service discovery config in one of the clients brought down service discovery globally when a dependent client went down.
A configuration change rolled out to GitHub.com databases broke the way hosts answered routing-service health-check pings, so the production read-only endpoint was marked unhealthy and inaccessible.

A configuration change intended to address an uptick in demand for metadata storage overloaded part of the blob lookup system, causing a cascading failure with user-visible service impact to Gmail, Google Photos, Google Drive.
An automated remote configuration change did not propagate fully. Web dynos could not be started.
PagerDuty deployed a DNS configuration change that impacted their container orchestration cluster, causing all services running there to be unable to resolve DNS.
A RDS hardware failure highlighted an incorrect MySQL configuration which resulted in major data loss in a financial system.
An unknown event caused a transformer to fail, and a PLC checking generator phase alignment failed, preventing backup generators from coming online, affecting EC2, EBS, RDS in EU West.

A bug in third-party datacenter control system code caused excessive interactions during a control-host failover, making the cooling control system unresponsive, causing EC2 servers to overheat and power off.
A partial switch misbehavior caused a cascading Byzantine failure which impacted API and dashboard availability for six hours 33 minutes.
GitHub experienced a disruption in the power at their primary datacenter.
A simultaneous failure of multiple redundant cooling systems in a datacenter impacted multiple Google Cloud services, causing customers to experience service unavailability.
A latent race condition in DynamoDB's DNS management left the regional endpoint with an empty record, cascading into EC2, Network Load Balancer, and Lambda for ~15 hours.

During a switch upgrade, an MLAG failover froze the network briefly, causing fileserver Pacemaker/Heartbeat/DRBD pairs to STONITH each other, leaving many pairs with both nodes powered off; recovery took over 5 hours.

A 43 second network partition during maintenance caused MySQL master failover, but the new master didn't have several seconds of writes propagated to it due to cross-continent latency, requiring 24+ hours of restoration work.
A combination of conflicting deployed versions and re-using a previously used flag bit caused a $460M trading loss.
Customers noticed per-organization IDs jumping by 32 after a Postgres HA upgrade promoted a follower to primary, due to sequence pre-allocation behavior.

Certificates valid for one year were computed as current date plus one year; on Feb 29 2012 this created certificates expiring Feb 29 2013, which were rejected as invalid, causing an Azure global outage lasting most of a day.
Backwards time flow from tracking a leap second caused weighted round-robin DNS resolver selection to panic and fail on some CNAME lookups.
Most Firefox add-ons stopped working when a certificate expired, disabling about 15,000 add-ons; recovery took 15-21 hours for most users.

At peak load, the primary database backed up with queued operations until it stopped catching up; a primary failover only bought temporary headroom, and CircleCI rebuilt tooling on the fly to clear a 17-hour backlog.

A foreign key on the scoped-tokens table hit max INT32, causing high failure rates for Actions and Pages and breaking scoped-token Git operations for 9h48m; mitigation required a long-running schema migration to INT64.

During the final rename step of a schema migration, a significant portion of MySQL read replicas entered a semaphore deadlock and crash-recovery, leaving too few healthy replicas to handle production reads.
A foreign key used a smaller data type than the primary key it referenced, causing an overflow when the primary key exceeded the allowable value, preventing new authorizations and deployments.

After a Postgres 17 upgrade, PGAudit was re-enabled based on staging testing; a routine migration triggered a pathological interaction where the extension hung holding critical locks and ignored timeout signals, blocking operations across the dashboard, mobile app, and API.

During debugging, a command intended to remove a small number of servers was issued with a typo, removing a much larger set that supported critical S3 systems, causing widespread outages across dependent AWS services.
A parser bug caused Cloudflare edge servers to return memory that contained private information such as HTTP cookies, authentication tokens, and HTTP POST bodies.
CPU exhaustion was caused by a single WAF rule with a poorly written regular expression causing excessive backtracking, leading to a global 27 minute downtime.
A content update containing undetected errors was deployed due to a bug in the deployment validator, causing an out-of-bounds memory read and a Windows crash on 8.5 million machines.

A Redis instance was migrated automatically by the cloud platform, causing it to incorrectly drop offline and forcing a cluster rebalance that triggered a cascading failure through Discord's real-time system, requiring a full service restart.
An influx of requests overloaded the database, causing replication to lag; a tired admin then deleted the wrong directory, losing six hours of data.
A critical Kubernetes cluster upgrade failed because node metadata changed between versions, bringing down workload networking for over 5 hours.
A combination of factors caused a large number of users to be disconnected; the mass reconnection attempt exceeded database capacity and caused cascading connection failures for up to 2 hours.
A manual database operation was performed incorrectly, missing a dependency, causing the Stripe API to go down for 90 minutes.

A temporary network partition in the Redis cluster used for billing caused a massive resynchronization; the overloaded master crashed and restarted read-only, and the auto-recharge system retried repeatedly, resulting in multiple duplicate charges to customers.
GitHub experienced a DDoS attack, hitting the website with 1.35Tbps of traffic.

Elastic Cloud customers with deployments in the AWS eu-west-1 region experienced severely degraded access to their clusters for roughly 3 hours, including a 20 minute period of complete unavailability.
A global outage occurred due to an undiscovered software bug that surfaced when it was triggered by a valid customer configuration change.
Honeycomb experienced a total outage impacting all user-facing components for over an hour, during which no data could be processed or accessed.
An attacker group gained access to a third-party support engineer's laptop, leading to a security compromise investigation.
Queues for requests and responses in a Redis cache became corrupted and out of sequence, leading to some requests revealing other users' data, including app activity and billing info.

A policy change executed as part of a standard security controls review inadvertently blocked access to resources beyond its intended scope, disrupting login and service access for a subset of customers.
A cascading error from an adjacent service led to the merchant authentication service being overloaded, impacting merchants for about 2 hours.

A deploy intended as a small bugfix also upgraded live databases on running production machines; an overflow in signed 32-bit integer IDs then caused database operations to fail, leading Etsy to take the site down during the upgrade.
A scheduled OS upgrade appears to have caused some machines to be wiped, which took out some databases.
A database capacity downgrade intended to minimize AWS spend resulted in insufficient capacity to support customers at peak load, leading to cascading collapse of dependent servers.
A cascading failure occurred due to a request queue overloading existing, insufficient database capacity, attributed to inadequate capacity planning and monitoring.

MongoDB fell over under load when it ran out of memory due to a query pattern with low data locality, and a lack of monitoring let the load go undetected until it became catastrophic, causing 17 hours of downtime.
The primary database became inconsistent with all replicas, undetected until a query failed, caused by a MySQL bug that sometimes caused ORDER BY to be ignored.
Transaction ID wraparound in Postgres caused a partial outage lasting a day and a half.
Transaction ID wraparound in Postgres caused Sentry to go down for most of a working day.
Strava hit the signed integer limit on a primary key, causing uploads to fail.

Secondary MongoDB servers became overloaded, and while troubleshooting, a change accidentally sent all secondary traffic to the primary MongoDB server, overloading it as well and worsening the outage.
A Cassandra cluster crashed, and the failure percolated to various data producers that ended up blocking on queue insert operations, eventually leading to failure of the entire application.

Operations on Manta were blocked because a lock could not be obtained on PostgreSQL metadata servers, due to transaction wraparound maintenance combined with a query that unnecessarily took a global lock.

An operator using a tool with lax input validation forgot a flag and rebooted all servers in a datacenter instead of a small maintenance subset, causing a 2.5 hour outage across all customer instances.
An EBS outage in one availability zone was mitigated by migrating workloads to other availability zones.
A database hit an integer limit, leaving the service in read-only mode.
Roblox experienced a 73 hour outage due to issues with Consul streaming and BoltDB.
Network saturation in cloud provider traffic gateways caused packet loss; an attempt to scale up capacity caused additional issues.

The Order Management System collapsed when a large order for a penny stock was divided into far more individual trades than typical, triggering a failure not previously encountered by the OMS provider.
